message.content:
**Order filled:** 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 (≈$9,801).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. Apple reported **net income of $93,736 million for fiscal 2024**, down from $96,995 million in fiscal 2023 — but that decline is almost entirely explained by a one-time, non-cash-like tax event: a $10.2 billion net income tax charge in Q4 2024 stemming from the European Court of Justice's September 10, 2024 ruling confirming the EU State Aid Decision, which pushed the effective tax rate from 14.7% to 24.1%. Underlying operations improved: total net sales rose 2% to $391,035 million, operating income grew 7.8% to $123,216 million, gross margin expanded from 44.1% to 46.2%, Services revenue grew 13% to $96,169 million at a 73.9% gross margin, and operating cash flow was a robust $118,254 million, with diluted EPS of $6.08. The main soft spot was Greater China, where net sales fell 8% to $66,952 million. I checked the live quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask) and placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.75 — about $9,801, inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, using existing cash ($50,000) with no funds moved out of the account. The order filled at $222.75.
